  "summary": "In this letter dated 8 June 1963, M. R. Masani responds to Acharya J. B. Kripalani's six-point minimum programme for inter-opposition unity. Masani says he appreciates Kripalani's efforts but cannot predict the Swatantra Party's response before its Central Organising Committee and Parliamentary Board meet. He doubts that a formal bloc or front can successfully commit itself to a minimum programme, given the difficulties of securing agreement among the parties.\n\nMasani instead advocates continued joint action on agreed issues, citing cooperation among the Swatantra Party, P.S.P., Jan Sangh and Socialist Party during and after the previous Parliament, as well as spontaneous cooperation in the Amroha and Rajkot by-elections. Looking ahead to the 1967 election, he proposes bilateral discussions among opposition parties while rejecting an attempt at ideological agreement at that stage. He closes by offering to meet Kripalani and Rajaji, along with two other political leaders, anywhere in India. The PDF contains three copies of the same two-page letter.",

      "He argues that a formal opposition bloc or front committed to a minimum programme would face serious difficulties.",
      "He prefers joint action on agreed issues, pointing to cooperation among several opposition parties and at the Amroha and Rajkot by-elections.",
      "He recommends beginning bilateral discussions aimed at an electoral understanding for 1967.",
      "He considers ideological agreement premature but remains willing to support further efforts toward unity.",
      "He offers to participate in a meeting with Kripalani and Rajaji, together with two other leaders."
